speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within follicle-bearing epithelium, combined with a firm, non-tender, crusted plaque on both the genital and hand skin, strongly raises suspicion for Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma. Given the multifocal nature of the lesions, have you recently had any significant sun exposure or history of severe burns?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma. The patient's history of heavy smoking, age, African origin (higher risk for specific subtypes), and the biopsy findings of nuclear hyperchromasia and increased mitotic figures confirm this diagnosis. The multifocal presentation on the hand and penis is consistent with chronic sun exposure and tobacco-related carcinogenesis.
